question: Who pioneered the practice of placing critically ill soldiers close to nursing stations?
explanation: Florence Nightingale grouped the most severely wounded soldiers nearest the nursing station during the Crimean War to ensure close observation. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why did Florence Nightingale place critically ill patients near the nurses' station?

options.A: To limit the spread of airborne hospital infections
options.B: To ensure doctors could access them first
options.C: To provide continuous observation and care
options.D: To keep them away from noisy recovery wards

explanation: Grouping unstable patients near the nursing station allowed nurses to monitor them constantly and intervene rapidly when changes occurred. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which major disease outbreak drove the early development of mechanical ventilation?
explanation: The polio epidemics of the mid-20th century caused widespread respiratory paralysis, which forced hospitals to develop mechanical ventilation methods. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h2)

question: What role did nursing play during the polio epidemics regarding respiratory support?

options.A: Manufacturing iron lung machines in hospital basements
options.B: Performing emergency spinal tap procedures on all admissions
options.C: Providing continuous manual ventilation and airway management
options.D: Prescribing muscle relaxants to ease breathing difficulties

explanation: Nurses worked around the clock performing manual ventilation and managing tracheostomies when mechanical iron lungs failed. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h2)

question: Where was the first centralized intensive care ward established during a polio outbreak?
explanation: The first centralized respiratory care ward was established in Copenhagen in 1953 by Bjorn Ibsen during a severe polio epidemic. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h3)

question: What was the main advantage of centralizing critically ill patients into one ward?

options.A: Eliminating the need for physician oversight during night shifts
options.B: Allowing families to visit patients without restriction
options.C: Reducing the overall cost of hospital construction and maintenance
options.D: Pooling specialized equipment and expert nursing staff in one location

explanation: Centralizing critical patients allowed hospitals to concentrate scarce resources like ventilators and specially trained nurses where they were needed most. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h3)

question: What specialized unit was created in the 1960s specifically for heart attack patients?
explanation: Coronary Care Units were established in the 1960s to monitor heart attack patients continuously and treat lethal arrhythmias immediately. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h4)

question: Why did the introduction of coronary care units drastically reduce heart attack mortality?

options.A: High doses of intravenous antibiotics prevented secondary infections
options.B: Doctors developed surgical cures for blocked coronary arteries
options.C: Continuous ECG monitoring allowed immediate intervention for fatal arrhythmias
options.D: Patients were kept completely unconscious to rest their hearts

explanation: Continuous cardiac monitoring enabled nurses and doctors to catch ventricular fibrillation early and apply defibrillation before irreversible damage occurred. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h4)

question: When was the American Association of Critical-Care Nurses founded to formalize the specialty?
explanation: The AACN was founded in 1969 to set professional standards and provide formal education for nurses working in intensive care environments. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h5)

question: What drove the transformation of critical care nursing into a distinct formal specialty?

options.A: The desire of physicians to delegate all administrative paperwork
options.B: The demand from hospital administrators for lower staffing costs
options.C: The reduction in nursing school enrollment numbers worldwide
options.D: The complexity of advanced life support technology and monitoring systems

explanation: Advanced monitors, ventilators, and vasoactive medications required nurses to possess specialized physiological knowledge beyond basic general nursing training. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h5)

question: Which device provides real-time, beat-to-beat blood pressure tracking in the ICU?
explanation: An arterial catheter inserted into a peripheral artery provides continuous, beat-to-beat blood pressure monitoring for unstable patients. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h6)

question: How do modern electronic health records improve patient safety in critical care units?

options.A: By automatically diagnosing complications before symptoms appear
options.B: By allowing family members to update patient charts from home
options.C: By integrating alarms, lab values, and medication orders into one system
options.D: By replacing the need for bedside physical assessments by nurses

explanation: Integrated digital systems help reduce medication and monitoring errors by centralizing critical patient data in real time. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is a primary focus for advancing critical care nursing practice in Nigeria today?

options.A: Eliminating the need for mechanical ventilators in emergency wards
options.B: Transitioning entirely to outpatient surgical care models
options.C: Replacing all bedside nurses with automated robotic systems
options.D: Expanding specialized training programs and improving resource management

explanation: Nigerian critical care development emphasizes specialized training and overcoming local resource challenges to improve patient survival rates. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h7)

question: How can artificial intelligence predictive analytics assist intensive care unit nurses?

options.A: By taking over direct physical patient hygiene and turning schedules
options.B: By alerting staff to clinical deterioration before overt symptoms appear
options.C: By discharging stable patients without requiring nursing sign-off
options.D: By replacing physician rounds with automated electronic prescriptions

explanation: Predictive analytics analyze continuous monitor data to warn nurses of complications like sepsis or shock hours ahead of time. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h7)
